creative_treatments.title: Fresh creative can be ready without replacing ads that still work
creative_treatments.content_opportunity: Explore the distinction Carmen made between having new creative available monthly and deciding when live ads should change. Her explanation contrasted keeping working creative with refreshing Funktastic conversion ads when performance declined. The owner's question gives this a practical purpose: understanding what ongoing management is doing between visible replacements.
creative_treatments.strategic_rationale: Makes performance-led management judgment understandable without equating service value with a fixed number of changes or making unsupported claims about algorithms.
creative_treatments.audience: Wedding-business owners who want to understand how an advertising partner decides when to introduce new creative.
creative_treatments.core_perspective: Creative production and live creative replacement can follow different schedules; the availability of something new does not by itself make replacing a working ad the right decision.
creative_treatments.tension: An owner wants visibility into creative work, while the practitioner must decide whether a change is warranted by campaign behavior.
creative_treatments.wia_expertise_in_action: Carmen explained that she generally avoided changing working creative and described refreshing some Funktastic conversion creative because performance was declining. Marisa asked about cadence and requested a more dependable review opportunity; Whitney offered a recurring strategy meeting.
creative_treatments.service_relevance: The exchange illustrates Carmen's management reasoning in this account, not a universal monthly creative entitlement or reporting cadence.
creative_treatments.selection_reason: The concrete distinction between creative readiness and deployment reveals judgment that a monthly-refresh tip would miss. The communication issue is retained separately as internal learning rather than turned into a second public angle.
